title: Heraclea Lyncestis founded
description: Philip II of Macedon founds a town to hold the newly conquered region of Lyncestis.

title: Earthquake destroys Scupi
description: An earthquake ruins the Roman city of Scupi, the forerunner of Skopje.

title: Clement comes to Ohrid
description: Clement, a pupil of Cyril and Methodius, is sent to teach in the region and founds the Ohrid Literary School of Slavic writing.

title: Archbishopric of Ohrid
description: After conquering the state of Tsar Samuel, Basil II sets up an autonomous archbishopric at Ohrid that lasts until 1767.

title: Church of St. Panteleimon at Nerezi
description: A Komnenian prince founds a monastery church whose frescoes are among the finest works of Byzantine painting.

title: Serbia takes Skopje
description: King Stefan Milutin captures Skopje from the Byzantines, and it later becomes the Serbian capital.

title: Ottomans take Skopje
description: Skopje falls to the Ottomans, who rule it as Üsküb for more than five centuries.

title: Mustafa Pasha Mosque
description: The vizier Mustafa Pasha builds a mosque above the Old Bazaar of Skopje, then a growing Ottoman trading town.

title: Burning of Skopje
description: The Austrian general Piccolomini sets fire to plague-stricken Skopje, which does not recover for two centuries.

title: Archbishopric of Ohrid abolished
description: The sultan dissolves the archbishopric and places its dioceses under the Patriarch of Constantinople.

title: Internal Macedonian Revolutionary Organization founded
description: Six men found a secret society to win autonomy for Macedonia from the Ottoman Empire.

title: Ilinden Uprising
description: Insurgents rise against Ottoman rule and proclaim a republic at Kruševo that lasts ten days.

title: On Macedonian Matters
description: Krste Misirkov publishes a book arguing for a separate Macedonian nation and literary language.

title: Ohrid–Debar uprising
description: Bulgarian and Albanian bands rise against Serbia, which had taken the region from the Ottomans in the Balkan Wars, and are put down within two weeks.

title: Breakthrough at Dobro Pole
description: Serbian and French troops break the Bulgarian line on the Macedonian front, and Bulgaria leaves the war two weeks later.

title: Comintern recognises a Macedonian nation
description: The Communist International adopts a resolution recognising the Macedonians as a separate nation with their own language.

title: Partisan uprising begins
description: Partisans attack the Bulgarian police station in Prilep, the date kept as the start of the anti-fascist struggle.

title: Deportation of the Jews of Macedonia
description: Bulgarian authorities round up more than 7,000 Jews, hold them in a tobacco warehouse in Skopje and hand them to the Germans, who kill almost all at Treblinka.

title: First session of ASNOM
description: A Partisan assembly proclaims a Macedonian state within federal Yugoslavia with Macedonian as its official language.

title: Macedonian alphabet adopted
description: A commission agrees and the government adopts a Cyrillic alphabet of thirty-one letters, the basis of the standard Macedonian language.

title: Skopje earthquake
description: An earthquake kills more than 1,000 people and destroys most of Skopje, which is rebuilt with international help.

title: Macedonian Orthodox Church declares autocephaly
description: On the two hundredth anniversary of the abolition of the Archbishopric of Ohrid the church declares itself independent of the Serbian Orthodox Church.

title: Independence referendum
description: Voters back independence from Yugoslavia, which the republic achieves without war.

title: Admission to the United Nations
description: The country joins the United Nations under the provisional name the former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia because of the dispute with Greece.

title: Ohrid Agreement
description: The government and ethnic Albanian parties end a months-long insurgency with an agreement widening the rights of the Albanian minority.

title: Prespa Agreement
description: Greece and Macedonia agree that the country will be called North Macedonia, ending a dispute that had run since 1991.

title: Name changed to North Macedonia
description: The new name comes into force, clearing the way for membership of NATO.
